title: Geometric Frobenius scalar on each signed coefficient section
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Set $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $B=\mathcal O_E$ or $\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{n+1}$ for $n\ge0$. Use the completed integral or finite coefficient sheaf and the signed tensor/dual line $B(m)_s$ [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Let $\Psi_m$ be restriction/coprojection along geometric Frobenius followed by the recorded signed line comparison [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport, def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. For every $m\in\mathbf Z$ and section $x\in\Gamma(s,B(m)_s)$, $\Psi_m(x)=(\operatorname{inverse}(q)^{\max(m,0)}q^{\max(-m,0)})x$, where the scalar acts through the actual constant-section map (and its quotient-compatible completion integrally). The explicit section formulas are [def-pur-point-cyclotomic-section-data].

source.place: (2.2), pp. 280-281 (root action, tensor powers, duals); geometric convention in Deligne Weil II (1.1.7), pp. 150-151; returned item steps 5-7

proof.text: By [lem-pur-point-root-limit-cyclotomic-action] geometric restriction/comparison sends every completed root section to q inverse times that section. The coordinate theorem supplies a compatible primitive root basis and trivializations of the signed coefficient lines. The constant comparisons fix all scalar sections, including for completed coefficients by their finite projections.

The tensor comparison of [lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom] sends the inverse image of a pure tensor to the tensor of the inverse images, including for extension of coefficients and iterated powers. Restriction of a tensor section $x\otimes y$ is $\operatorname{res}_g(x)\otimes\operatorname{res}_g(y)$, by the construction of a sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. In the evaluation chart of [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural] the coprojections are identities, so this formula also computes $\sigma$ followed by the tensor comparison. Now the definition [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists] (2) gives
$\Psi_1^{\mathcal O_E}(e\otimes1)=(q^{-1}e)\otimes1=q^{-1}e_{\mathcal O_E}$,
and its finite coefficient extension gives $\Psi_1^{A_{E,n}}(e_B)=q^{-1}e_B$. Clause (3) of that definition and the same pure-tensor formula give, for $m\ge1$,
$\Psi_{m+1}^B(e_{m,B}\otimes e_B)=\Psi_m^B(e_{m,B})\otimes\Psi_1^B(e_B)$.
Induction starting at $m=1$ now gives $\Psi_m^B(e_{m,B})=q^{-m}e_{m,B}$ for all $m>0$: the induction step multiplies $q^{-m}$ by $q^{-1}$. Only these specified pure tensor sections are used, not a claim that global sections preserve arbitrary tensor products.

source.place: (2.2), pp. 280-281; explicit pro-etale section calculation by the worker; geometric convention: Deligne Weil II (1.1.7), pp. 150-151

proof.text:
Fix $r>0$. By [lem-pur-point-tate-root-coordinates], a section of the sheaf dual $B(-r)_s$ is a $B$-linear functional on the free line $B e_{r,B}$, determined by its value at $e_{r,B}$. The Hom comparison in [lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom] sends an inverse-image functional to that functional on inverse-image local sections. Restriction of a sheaf-Hom section satisfies $(\operatorname{res}_g\varphi)(\operatorname{res}_g x)=\operatorname{res}_g(\varphi(x))$, by the definition of sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Evaluate clause (3) of [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists], namely $c_B\circ(g^{-1}\varphi)\circ(\tau_r^B)^{-1}$, on $\tau_r^B(\sigma x)$. The inverse cancels $\tau_r^B$; the Hom comparison and the evaluation identity give $c_B\sigma(\varphi(x))=\varphi(x)$ by the preceding coefficient calculation. Hence
$\Psi_{-r}^B(\varphi)(\Psi_r^B(x))=\varphi(x)$.
The preceding positive formula and the coordinate lemma show that $\Psi_r^B$ is the invertible scalar $q^{-r}$. Substituting $x=(\Psi_r^B)^{-1}y$ yields $\Psi_{-r}^B(\varphi)=\varphi\circ(\Psi_r^B)^{-1}$. In particular its value for $\varphi=e_{-r,B}$ at $e_{r,B}$ is $e_{-r,B}(q^r e_{r,B})=q^r$.

source.place: (2.2), pp. 280-281; explicit pro-etale section calculation by the worker; geometric convention: Deligne Weil II (1.1.7), pp. 150-151

proof.text: For each integer $m$, [lem-pur-point-tate-root-coordinates] identifies all sections with $B e_{m,B}$. The scalar formula for $\sigma$ in [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural] and the $B_s$-linearity of $\tau_m^B$ in [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists] imply $\Psi_m^B(bx)=b\Psi_m^B(x)$. For $m=0$ the coefficient calculation gives the result; for $m>0$ use the tensor induction; for $m=-r<0$ the dual calculation and determination by evaluation at $e_{r,B}$ give $\Psi_{-r}^B(e_{-r,B})=q^r e_{-r,B}$. Thus in all cases $\Psi_m^B(b e_{m,B})=b q^{-m}e_{m,B}$. The unit $q$ of step 2 remains a unit under $\mathbf Z_\ell\to B$, so every displayed signed power is defined, including in the finite, possibly nonreduced ring $A_{E,n}$.

from.place: geometric Frobenius acts on E(1) by q inverse, on E(m) by q to minus m, and actions commute with finite reduction; signed scalar part

lean.statement:
theorem signed_section_scalar (hl : l ≠ D.p) (a : Option ℕ) (m : ℤ)
    (x : (line D l E a m).val.obj (op (finalObject D))) :
    action D l E a m x =
      scale D l E a m (Ring.inverse (D.q : scalars l E a) ^ m.toNat *
        (D.q : scalars l E a) ^ (-m).toNat) x
